builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CGSpec: Consistency-Guided Speculative Decoding with Overlap-Aware Verification Scheduling for Edge-Cloud Inference
summary: CGSpec replaces standard collaborative speculative decoding with static speculative budgets and naive shared-verifier scheduling by adding divergence-guided adaptive budgets, nomination-and-competition tree construction, and overlap-aware request scheduling. It costs additional verifier-side bookkeeping, client return-time estimation, and coordination logic between edge drafters and the cloud verifier. It can fail when divergence estimates misjudge draft-target agreement, when network heterogeneity invalidates return-time predictions, or in single-client deployments where the scheduling gains do not materialize.
rationale: The method targets multi-client edge-cloud inference with a shared verifier, an infrastructure shape the reader does not operate, so it is worth tracking but not deployable on a single 24 GB GPU.
technique: Consistency-guided multi-client speculative decoding with verification scheduling

claims.statement: CGSpec replaces standard collaborative speculative decoding with static speculative budgets and naive shared-verifier scheduling by adding divergence-guided adaptive budgets, nomination-and-competition tree construction, and overlap-aware request scheduling. It costs additional verifier-side bookkeeping, client return-time estimation, and coordination logic between edge drafters and the cloud verifier. It can fail when divergence estimates misjudge draft-target agreement, when network heterogeneity invalidates return-time predictions, or in single-client deployments where the scheduling gains do not materialize.

Improves system throughput by 12.2% (8 clients) and 10.2% (16 clients) over SOTA baselines, and mean client throughput by 14.0% and 33.0%, across 24 configurations with four model pairs and three datasets.
